title: Activity-log query endpoints strictly scope results to the caller's organization
description: GET /api/activity-logs and its /dashboard summary both build their MongoDB filter from req.orgId server-side. Verify a user from one org can never retrieve another org's log entries, including via query-parameter manipulation.
preconditions: ActivityLog entries seeded for two distinct organizations, Org A and Org B
Test user belonging only to Org A
steps: Authenticate as the Org A user and call GET /api/activity-logs with no filters.
Attempt to pass Org B's organizationId, a Org-B resourceId, or a Org-B projectId as query parameters on both endpoints.
Confirm which entries are returned in each case.
expectedResult: Both endpoints only ever return entries where organizationId matches req.orgId (the $or: [{organizationId: req.orgId}, {organizationId: orgIdStr}] filter in vibrantix-backend/src/modules/activity/activity-logs.routes.js lines 27-33 and 84-88) — Org B's entries are never returned to the Org A caller under any combination of client-supplied query parameters, since organizationId is derived from the authenticated session, not from client input.

title: Reading the audit trail is itself captured as a compliance.audit_log.accessed event
description: activity-logs.routes.js logs a meta-event every time GET /api/activity-logs or its dashboard summary is called, recording who queried the log and with what filters — so access to the audit trail is itself forensically traceable.
steps: Authenticate as an org user and call GET /api/activity-logs?module=policy.
Inspect the log entries emitted by these two calls themselves (not the entries they returned in the response body).
expectedResult: Each call produces a type: "compliance", event: "compliance.audit_log.accessed" entry recording accessedBy (req.userId), orgId, the filters applied (module/resourceType/action), and either resultCount + totalMatched (list endpoint) or queryType: "dashboard_summary" (dashboard endpoint) — per vibrantix-backend/src/modules/activity/activity-logs.routes.js lines 55-63 and 98-105.

title: Cross-organization role mutation attempts are captured as authz.cross_org.attempt security events
description: role.controller.js checks that a custom role's organizationId matches the caller's org before allowing update/delete, and logs a distinct security event when that check fails. Verify this IDOR guard is both enforced and logged with full attribution.
preconditions: Custom role belonging to Org B, whose _id is known/guessed by an Org A user
steps: As an authenticated user in Org A, call PUT /api/roles/:id where :id is a custom role belonging to Org B.
Repeat with DELETE /api/roles/:id against the same Org B role.
Inspect the log entry emitted for each attempt.
expectedResult: Each attempt emits a type: "security", event: "authz.cross_org.attempt" entry with userId, email, requestingOrgId, targetOrgId, resource (req.path), action (HTTP method), and ip (vibrantix-backend/src/modules/rbac/role.controller.js lines 142-152 for update, 225-236 for delete) before the request is rejected with 403 — the cross-tenant IDOR attempt against the role model is captured in the audit trail, not just silently blocked.
